articles.title: Matching The Milbank Scale Before Most Of Biglaw — See Also
articles.content:
当其他大律所仍在等待Cravath律师事务所的动向时，麦库尔·史密斯律师事务所（McKool Smith）直接匹配了Milbank的薪资水平——这家德州审判大咖宣布将提高律师助理的薪资10,000至20,000美元，从2024年1月1日起生效。在律所薪资竞赛中，"Kool"的孩子总是最后出手，但每次都准。

**刑法教育从早就开始**：宾夕法尼亚州立大学某兄弟会可卡因交易案，导致一位潜在法学生失去了入学资格。

**降低标准？在本届政府中？**：美国教育部开始废除美国律师协会（ABA）对法学院的认证程序。难道谁都没想到，向政府的要求让步会引发反噬？

**律师助理薪资评分表**：回顾本周期中那些敢于发放奖金和加薪的律所。

**公共健康领域工作激动人心**：这正是为什么我们需要像这样的优秀学校，去培养对卫生法感兴趣的人才。

**你在做笔记吗？**：一名前检察官被指控在离职后，留下了大量的书面记录，其中包含对前雇主的暴力威胁。

（原文首发于Above the Law）
articles.summary:
While The Rest Of Biglaw Waits On Cravath, McKool Smith Just Matched Milbank: The Texas trial powerhouse is raising associate salaries $10K to $20K — effective January 1. The ‘Kool’ kids always come through eventually.

Crim Law Lessons Start Early: Penn State frat coke ring costs prospective law student their slot.

Lowering Standards? In This Administration?: The Department of Education begins process of ending ABA law school accreditation. Who could have guessed that giving in to the administration’s demands would backfire?

The Associate Compensation Scorecard: Catch up with the firms brave enough to issue bonuses and raises this cycle.

It’s A Wild Time To Be Working In Public Health: That’s why we need great schools like this for those interested in health law.

Is You Taking Notes?: Former prosecutor accused of leaving a robust written record of violent threats against former bosses.

articles.title: Supreme Court Confirmation Isn’t Always A Sure Thing — Just Ask The First Man To Lose One
articles.content: **每日趣味问答：哪位最高法院大法官候选人在乔治·华盛顿任命期间已开始担任首席大法官，但后被参议院否决？** **提示：**这是参议院首次拒绝确认最高法院大法官提名，他138天的任期也是历史上最短的首席大法官任期。他因一场激烈演讲反对与英国的争议性条约而得罪了刚刚投票批准该条约的联邦党参议员，最终落选。 **答案见下一页。** *原文链接：最高法院确认并非总是顺利——问问首位被否决的人，首发于《法律之上》。*
articles.summary:
Ed. Note: Welcome to our daily feature Trivia Question of the Day!

Which Supreme Court nominee was already serving as chief justice — installed by George Washington during a Senate recess and presiding over a full term — when the Senate came back, took up his nomination, and rejected him outright?

Hint: It was the first time the Senate ever refused to confirm a Supreme Court nominee, and his 138 days remain the shortest tenure of any chief justice in history. What sank him was a fiery speech he’d given back home denouncing a controversial treaty with Great Britain, enraging the Federalist senators who had just voted to ratify it.
See the answer on the next page.

articles.title: How To Audit Your Law Firm Website For AI Readability
articles.content:
随着生成式人工智能（GenAI）的出现，这种能够直接回答用户问题的技术促使人们开始关注GEO（生成引擎优化），这与更传统的SEO（搜索引擎优化）实践密切相关。虽然GEO和SEO通常可以相辅相成，但在某些情况下，为了实现最大化的AI可读性，律所网站可能需要进行一些针对性的调整。AI可读性审核能够帮助您（或数字营销团队）识别这些需要调整的领域，并进行相应的优化。

进行律所网站AI可读性审核的许多步骤将围绕大语言模型（LLM）的特殊需求及其“阅读”网站和收集（处理）数据的实际方式展开。然而，某些情况下，您可能需要根据审核结果进行的调整，可能会影响网站在普通人类访客（即潜在客户）眼中的表现。这一交集在移动网站优化方面尤为明显。谷歌已多年将移动优化特性在搜索引擎结果页面（SERPs）中的权重不断加大，理由是移动搜索占搜索活动的比例越来越大，因此优先考虑满足移动用户需求的网站。

LLM将对移动就绪型网页设计的偏好进一步放大。为了让律所内容更有可能被AI搜索工具阅读和引用，您需要双重检查以下内容：记住，当前的LLM系统是在移动优先时代构建的，因此它们会将移动屏幕尺寸和移动浏览器功能作为“默认”假设，并相应地优化。

搜索引擎营销人员多年来一直在宣扬结构化数据的好处。虽然对人类访客不可见，但结构化数据（通常通过行业标准Schema标签系统实现）对帮助搜索引擎理解网站内容和页面之间的关系非常有用。数据标记（您需要查找和检查JSON-LD文件）有助于索引，确保网络爬虫能够对网站的每个页面进行分类。这一索引功能使搜索算法能够更轻松地根据您为页面选择的Schema“标签”解释页面内容，搜索引擎不仅知道页面说的是什么，还知道页面的类型（帮助页面、个人简介等）。通常结果是更好的（更准确的）可检索性，这正是您希望需要法律服务的人能够找到律所网站的效果。

搜索引擎专家对Schema标记在LLM搜索结果中的核心地位进行了争论，特别是与传统SERP排名的比较。一些专家自信地声称Schema标记对AI可读性的重要性甚至超过传统搜索引擎索引，而使用与否的测试在谷歌的AI概述中产生了“有前景但不确定”的结果。Schema标签对AI可读性的影响程度，以及这些影响如何转化为引用链接的包含情况，是一个有趣的智力谜题。然而，您不需要解决这个谜题即可进行AI可读性审核。部分答案可能是移动目标，因为LLM和搜索引擎算法（其结果有时被纳入生成答案的过程中）正在不断修订，这些变化通常意味着对各种因素进行微调，以确定响应查询时呈现的可能网站。

我们在关注这些问题时忽略的实际核心是，结构化数据没有任何弊端。律所使用它没有任何损失。结构化数据标记是一种低成本、高回报且风险几乎为零的干预措施。确保网站上的所有页面都符合Schema标签的最佳实践，并开始建立网站的权威性，以便在JSON-LD发展到需要更改时更容易进行更新。

至少，律所网站应包含以下页面的Schema标签：

您可能还需要对“关于”页面和文章页面应用结构化数据标记，特别是如果您将博客作为SEO/GEO内容策略的重要组成部分。要进一步提升Schema标签，还可以将其应用到实践领域页面。

任何AI可读性审核都应包括针对LLM的特定功能检查，即llms.txt文件。这些文本文件以Markdown格式编写，并添加到网站的根目录中。llms.txt文件为LLM扫描网站时提供“备忘单”信息，也可以将其视为一种“地图”，帮助LLM在扫描内容时定位。目标是增强AI可读性，就像sitemap.xml为传统网络爬虫提高可读性一样。虽然llms.txt的包含可能需要一段时间才能产生可衡量的收益，但合理的期望是，随着我们进入本年度的剩余时间，AI工具将逐渐更加依赖其自身的搜索算法（独立于其经常整合到其流程中的传统网络搜索结果）。

只要您使用结构化数据标识FAQs页面并为LLM提供律所网站的指南，您可能还想查看内容，以确保其符合您已确定为重要的类别（即数据类型）。为了最大化投资回报，您可以将此步骤与检查传统搜索引擎和LLM在评估网站质量时寻找的重要“权威”信号结合起来。显然，您希望在律所的指定FAQs页面上回答真正常见的问题，并以问答形式呈现。然而，不要将“直接答案”格式留在FAQs页面上！确保您的博客文章甚至描述实践领域的页面包含针对客户访问您的实践时常见问题的精简答案，如律所的运作方式和处理的案件类型。如果您认为这些答案看起来有些像谷歌搜索结果页面中偶尔出现的“精选摘要”部分，那么您走在了正确的道路上！

通过在多个位置提及您的律所，可以增强LocalBusiness Schema的效果。至少，律所名称应出现在每个页面上；强行将其放入不自然的位置并非改进，但在审查网站现有内容时，寻找逻辑上需要再次提及您的律所的地方，并可能与内容策略师讨论未来创造更多这样的机会。当然，提及个别律师也很重要：他们的声誉就是您的声誉！确保博客页面在律师是合伙人或律所律师时给予署名，并通过强调其当前重点和过去成就的个人简介，将律所名称与律师的数字存在联系起来。

作为实践领域的专家，您不需要像在法庭申论那样为律所网站上公布的信息提供引用。然而，搜索引擎和LLM都会关注网站在书面内容中明确标识的来源（不妨直呼其名！）和链接到的页面。虽然很诱人地希望访客尽可能长时间地停留在您的网站上，但您需要将链接指向其他权威无可争议的页面。简单的策略是链接到政府网站上详细说明的法律法规或法院规则，这些对您的实践有规律性的影响；博客页面是随时间构建这种权威的有效工具，但也要审查实践领域页面的内容，寻找提升网站内容的机会。

搜索领域的格局在几年内发生了巨大变化。从谷歌作为搜索流量的唯一裁决者的时代，转变为多个生成式搜索引擎工具争夺地位的时代，这让许多律师感到有些喘不过气。然而，旧谚语仍然适用：变化越多，不变的越多。考虑与经验丰富的律所营销机构联系，他们不仅了解SEO和AI，还了解法律准确性和道德合规性的重要性。

AI可读性需要进行一些调整，以应对传统搜索引擎索引协议与LLM在数据访问和分类方面的差异，但网站整合准确“路标”和确保页面内容不仅与主题相关，而且能为机器人和人类提供证据，证明该站是核心问题的可信赖答案来源的基本原则仍然存在。AI可读性审核只是帮助确保律所网站将这些原则应用于LLM。

Annette Choti律师拥有超过20年的法律经验，是Law Quill的创始人兼CEO，该机构是一家为律所提供会员式法律营销服务的机构。Annette是畅销书《点击磁铁：律所数字营销终极指南》的作者，主持受欢迎的《法律营销休息室》播客，并创办了Click Magnet Academy，在那里她教授专业人士如何利用强大的LinkedIn平台。作为律师协会、法律协会和营销会议的受欢迎演讲者，Annette提供法律营销洞察力，并带来娱乐性。Annette曾从事戏剧和专业喜剧表演，这与法律领域并无不同。Annette可以在LinkedIn上找到，或通过电子邮件直接联系Annette@LawQuill.com。

本文最初发表于Above the Law。
articles.summary:
The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), adapted to provide direct answers to users’ questions, has led to an interest in GEO (generative engine optimization) that corresponds to and closely parallels the more established practices of SEO (search engine optimization). Often GEO and SEO can complement each other and work hand-in-hand, but there are a few areas in which achieving maximum AI readability may mean you need to make tailored “tweaks” to your law firm website. An AI readability audit helps you (or your digital marketing team) to identify those areas and apply any needed adjustments.

AI-Ready Web Design

Many of your steps toward auditing a law firm website for AI readability will be engineered around the specific needs of LLMs and the practicalities of the ways they “read” websites and gather (and process) data. In some instances, however, you will find that the adaptations you may want to make (depending on what your audit finds) can affect the way your site appears to the ordinary human viewers you hope may become your clients. One area in which this intersection can be particularly obvious is in mobile site optimization. Google has been increasing the weight the company’s eponymous search engine gives to mobile optimization features in determining how websites “rank” in search engine results pages (SERPs) for a few years now; the company’s contention has been that as mobile searches make up an ever larger share of search activity, it makes sense to prioritize sites that cater to mobile users.

LLMs take this preference for mobile-ready web design and amplify it. To give your law firm’s content the best chance of being read and referenced by AI search tools, double-check for the following:

  • “Mobile-first” design: This term gets tossed around a lot as a catchall for websites that offer some mobile-specific functionality. You want to apply a stricter definition during your audit. Take the “first” part of mobile-first seriously, and test each page of your website for readability and navigability, starting with the smallest screen size you think visitors might use (don’t forget the latest folding screens!).
  • Menus and navigation: While we are thinking about navigation, be sure to check not just the layout, but the function, of any menus (including header and sidebar menus) and their elements. Buttons and other features intended to help readers move from one place to another across your website get the same treatment. “Call-to-action” elements embedded in the middle of site pages are particularly prone to becoming unusable, invisible, or simply misplaced, in mobile browsing (this is another reason to work up from the smallest screen). Pay special attention to any features that are designed for desktop users to access via “hovering” their cursors: Are they obvious in mobile view? Do they function appropriately without a mouse to guide the cursor?
  • Loading speed: Sometimes pages will load at the same speed in a mobile browser as on a desktop. Often they will not. Mobile visitors who feel frustrated staring at a blank page, or one full of blank boxes where visual content theoretically might be, will frequently click away to continue their search for legal information and services elsewhere. Lower your bounce rate and keep prospective clients engaged by making sure your pages deliver the same low-friction experience, regardless of device.
  • Size matters: Review your site’s CSS to make sure that images, banners, and other design elements are designed for responsive sizing: You want your layout to prioritize proportions, not pixels. Be sure to check both portrait and landscape modes; responsible design should adjust seamlessly to match the orientation of the user’s device.

Remember: Current LLM systems were built in the mobile-first era. Expect them to take mobile screen sizes and mobile browser functions as their “default” assumptions and to prioritize accordingly.

If You Like It, Then You Should Have Put a Tag on It

Search engine marketers have been preaching the good news about structured data for years. While not visible to a website’s human visitors, structured data (typically via the industry-standard schema tag system) can be enormously helpful in helping search engines figure out what you think is on your website and how you see the site pages relating to one another.

What Are Schema Tags?

Data markup (you’ll be looking for, and examining, JSON-LD files) facilitates indexing by making sure that web crawlers can categorize each page of your website. This indexing function then makes it much easier for search algorithms to interpret your page content in light of the schema “tags” with which you have chosen to label it; the search engine knows not just what the page says, but the kind of document (help page, bio, etc.) the page is intended to be. The outcome, generally, is better (and more accurate) retrievability, which is exactly what you want if you are hoping the people who need your legal services will find your law firm website.

Is Structured Data Markup Really Crucial?

Search engine specialists have debated how central schema markup really is to LLM search results, particularly when compared to how structured data practices impact traditional SERP rankings. Some experts confidently assert that schema markup is even more important for AI readability than for traditional search engine indexing, while tests using vs. not using structured have yielded “promising, but inconclusive” results in Google’s AI Overviews.

The Realist’s Approach

The degree to which schema tags impact AI readability, and how those effects translate in terms of inclusion in citation links, is an interesting intellectual puzzle. However, it is not an intellectual puzzle you need to solve in order to audit your law firm website for AI readability. Some of the answers may be moving targets: both LLMs and the search engine algorithms whose results they sometimes incorporate in generating answers are constantly in revision, and often these changes amount to minor shifts in the relative weight assigned to each of the factors the program is considering in determining which possible websites to present in response to a query.

The practical bottom line we are all missing when we focus on these questions is that there is no downside to structured data. Your law firm has nothing to lose by using it. Structured data markup is a low-cost intervention with potentially high rewards and virtually no risk. Make sure all pages on your website are conforming to schema tag best practices now, and start building the website authority that will make it easier to integrate any updates later, if JSON-LD develops to the point where changes are needed.

What To Include

At a minimum, your law firm website should include schema tags for these pages:

  • FAQPage – ideal for the Q&A style LLMs seem to prefer
  • LegalService – so both search engines and AI tools know what kind of business your website belongs to
  • LocalBusiness – with information consistent across site pages (and ideally your law firm’s social media and other digital surfaces, as well) to optimize for local search

You will probably also want to apply structured data markup to an “about” page and an articles page, particularly if you are using blogs as an integral part of your SEO/GEO content strategy. To take your schema tags to the next level, apply the same technique to your practice area pages.

Talk to the Machine

One feature check specific to LLMs that any AI readability audit should include is an llms.txt. These text files are formatted in Markdown and added to a website’s root directory.

An llms.txt file provides “cheat sheet” information to LLMs as they scan your site; you could also think of them as a “map” of sorts to orient LLMs as they scan your content. The goal is to enhance AI readability in much the same way that sitemap.xml improves readability for traditional web crawlers. The inclusion of llms.txt may take a while to yield measurable dividends, but the reasonable expectation at this point is that AI tools will begin to rely more heavily on their own search algorithms (independent from the traditional web search results they often integrate in their processes) as we move through the rest of this year.

Answer Questions With Authority

As long as you are identifying FAQs pages using structured data and giving LLMs a guide to your law firm website, you will probably want to review the content to make sure that it is a good fit for the categories (i.e., data types) you have identified as important. To get the most bang for your buck, you can combine this step with checking for important “authority” signals that both traditional search engines and LLMs look for when evaluating website quality.

Q&A

Obviously you will want to answer questions that really are asked frequently on your law firm’s designated FAQs page, and you will probably want to do so in a question-and-answer format. However, you should not leave the “direct answer” format on the FAQs page! Make sure that your blog articles and even the pages describing your practice area(s) contain bite-sized answers to questions clients visiting your practice commonly have about how your law firm works and the kinds of cases you handle. If you think the answers look a little like something you might see showing up in the “featured snippets” sections Google sometimes drops into your search results pages, you are on the right track!

Say Your Name

Bolster the efficacy of your LocalBusiness schema by naming your own “entity” (your law firm) in multiple locations. At the very least, the law firm’s name should appear on every page; shoving it into locations where it does not fit naturally is not an improvement, but as you review the content already on your website, look for places where it would make logical sense to name your firm again, and maybe speak with your content strategist about ways to create more of those opportunities in the future. Of course, mentioning individual attorneys is also important: Their reputation is your reputation! Be sure that your blog pages give attribution when a partner or associate is the author, and connect the law firm name to the attorney’s own digital presence through a bio that highlights his or her current focus and past achievements.

Cite Your Sources

As an expert in your practice area(s), it makes sense that you would not need to cite the kinds of information that a law firm would typically post on a public website in the same way that you would need to provide references throughout a court brief. However, search engines and LLMs alike pay attention to the sources a website explicitly identifies in written content (go ahead and name drop!) and the pages to which the website links.

As tempting as it is to keep visitors on your own website as long as possible, you need links pointing off your site to other pages whose authority is undisputed. The easy strategy here is to link to the government websites detailing the legal codes or rules of court that have regular relevance to your practice; blog pages can be an effective tool for building this kind of authority over time, but be sure to review the content on your practice area pages as well to look for chances to “level up” your site content.

Work With a Search Specialist

The landscape of search has changed dramatically in just a few years. Transitioning from a world in which Google reigned the unquestioned arbiter of search traffic to one in which competing generative engine search tools jostle for position has left many attorneys feeling more than a little breathless from the whirlwind journey. At the same time, the old axiom holds true: The more things change, the more they stay the same. Consider visiting with an experienced law firm marketing agency that understands SEO and AI, as well as understands the importance of legal accuracy and ethics compliance. 

AI readability requires some adjustments to account for the differences between traditional search engine indexing protocols and LLMs in terms of data access and classification, but the underlying principles of integrating accurate “signposts” throughout your law firm website and ensuring that the content on your pages is not only topically relevant, but crafted to present bots as well as humans with evidence that your site is a trustworthy source of answers to core questions, remain in place. An AI readability audit simply helps to ensure that your law firm website is applying those principles for LLMs.

Annette Choti, Esq., has over two decades of legal experience and is the Founder & CEO of Law Quill, a concierge legal marketing agency for law firms.  Annette authored the bestselling book Click Magnet: The Ultimate Guide To Digital Marketing For Law Firms, hosts the popular Legal Marketing Lounge podcast, and founded Click Magnet Academy where she teaches professionals to leverage the powerful LinkedIn platform. As a sought after speaker for Bar Associations, Legal Associations, and Marketing Conferences, Annette provides legal marketing insight along with an entertaining twist. Annette used to do theatre and professional comedy, which is not so different from the legal field if we are all being honest. Annette can be found on LinkedIn or directly through email at Annette@LawQuill.com 

The post How To Audit Your Law Firm Website For AI Readability appeared first on Above the Law.

articles.title: Estonian Lawmaker Calls US Questionnaire To NATO ‘Unnecessary Stress Test’
articles.content:
米兰——五角大楼向北约盟国发送的问卷调查，旨在评估盟国对美方政策的支持程度，在欧洲引发了一定程度的不满。爱沙尼亚高级议员马克·米赫尔松（Marko Mihkelson）在接受《国防新闻》采访时表示，这一“新颖”的策略可能会分裂盟友联盟，并给对手可乘之机。

8月14日，彭博社首先报道了这份问卷，其中包括询问各国政府对美国政策的公开支持程度、与美方武器商的合作水平，以及是否允许使用本国的美军基地进行伊朗冲突行动等问题。该问卷据称与美军在欧洲的兵力部署评估有关。

“这是一种不必要的压力测试，处理方式也有问题。”米赫尔松说，作为爱沙尼亚议会外交委员会主席，他认为：“在评估兵力部署时，可以同时服务于美国国家利益和盟国利益。但这份问卷显然没有做到这一点。”

米赫尔松表示，北约国家收到问卷并非罕见，但通常是由北约总部发出，而非成员国单方面发起。不过，他并不感到特别意外，因为“美国政府现在处理问题的方式就是这样”。

爱沙尼亚议员认为，更好的做法是将这些问题提交到北约北大西洋理事会（NAC）会议上讨论，每个盟国都会派出领导人参与集体安全决策。米赫尔松虽然未亲眼见到问卷，但他了解到需要在8月27日之前提交回答，届时北约总部将在布鲁塞尔召开下一次NAC会议，美国国防政策副部长埃尔布里奇·科尔比（Elbridge Colby）将出席。

彭博社和卡塔尔半岛电视台报道称，一些欧洲官员对这份问卷提出了批评，尽管大多数盟国在公开场合采取了更为谨慎的态度。北约官员向《国防新闻》证实，华盛顿正与盟国合作进行兵力部署评估，但具体细节需要向美方确认。

挪威国防部发言人表示，他们在6月布鲁塞尔部长级会议上得知将有此类请求，目前正在审查问题并就美方提出的问题向美方作出回应。

芬兰总统亚历山大·斯图布（Alexander Stubb）在周一的新闻发布会上表示，他并不将美方的举动视为“压力”，因为“这是美国政府目前的运作方式”，彭博社报道说。

此外，德国国防部发言人在电子邮件中对《国防新闻》表示，柏林“也收到了美方关于参与其兵力部署评估的邀请”。发言人补充说，这为欧洲国家提供了一个机会，“继续与美国保持密切和信任的对话”，讨论共同的防务政策利益。

几个其他北约国家未回应置评请求。

前美驻北约大使伊沃·达尔达（Ivo Daalder，2009-2013年任职）在X平台上公开批评这份问卷，“这将忠诚度放在共同利益之上，分化盟友，削弱集体防卫，最终可能毁掉北约。”

一位美国官员拒绝直接回应问卷内容，但在接受《国防新闻》采访时表示：“特朗普总统已经明确表示，他对北约盟友在‘史诗之怒’行动期间支持不足感到非常失望，该行动通过解除伊朗核武装使整个世界更加安全。”

该官员补充说：“美国有数千名士兵驻扬在欧洲保护欧洲，但在这次冲突中，使用北约基地的请求被拒绝了。美国希望能够使用其在欧洲的基地来推进全球和欧洲安全。”

一位匿名的欧洲高级防务官员周三对半岛电视台表示：“美国政府一直混淆了北约议题与美国单边军事行动。这份问卷也反映了这种混淆。北约与中东无关。”

与此同时，在欧洲各国权衡如何回答美国的询问之际，米赫尔松表示，其他首都也在密切关注：莫斯科和北京。

“在这个非和平时期，欧洲发生重大战争的时刻，我们在言行上都不能采取任何步骤，让莫斯科或北京误以为北约内部分裂或未能集中精力应对边界上日益增长的威胁。”他说，“这对于避免这两个国家误判可见的分裂线至关重要。”

articles.title: When Partners Go On Vacation, Associates Should Relax A Little Too
articles.content:
律师事务所的合伙人在夏季休假是很常见的。合伙人比其他律师对自己的时间有更大的控制权，经过几十年的实践积累后，他们通常可以安心地离开一两周，而不用过于担心办公室发生的事情。当然，即使合伙人在海滩休息，工作也不会停止。律师助理依然需要为客户服务、按时完成任务并确保案件继续推进。

然而，我认为合伙人应该接受一个现实：当他们离开时，为他们工作的律师助理可能会稍微降低一些工作效率。我认为，在合理范围内，这是完全可以接受的。

在我的职业生涯中，我曾为多位老板工作过，每位老板对工作方式都有不同的期望。有些合伙人希望律师助理在特定的日子来办公室。有些则要求律师助理在特定时间到达，提供频繁的更新，或按照特定的程序处理任务。即使这些期望是合理的，但遵守它们仍需要一定的努力。

当负责这些期望的合伙人休假时，律师助理有时会稍微放松一些。也许平时来办公室工作的律师助理会选择在家工作几天。或许人们会稍微迟到一点或者早走一点。律师助理可能会花更长时间吃午餐，花更多时间与同事交谈，或者享受负责人暂时不在的事实。

合伙人应该允许这种情况发生。

需要明确的是，我是休假的坚定支持者。人们在定期远离工作时能更好地工作，而法律行业历来对让人们真正休假做得不好。律师应该利用他们的假期，旅行，陪伴家人，偶尔去一个不需要不断查看电子邮件的地方。合伙人不应该因为担心律师助理在自己不在时偷懒而避免休假。

实际上，律师助理应该将合伙人的休假视为一个放松自己的机会，即使他们并未正式请假。有时候，有一周时间无需在乎自己是否在上午9:30准时坐在办公桌前，这会令人感到新鲜。如果律师助理能在家完成任务，也许他们应该省去通勤时间。如果下午没有紧急工作，也许律师助理可以稍微早点下班。这些小小的自由可以带来假期的心理益处，而无需实际休假。

显然，这个原则也有其限制。律师助理不能因为监督律师在意大利而忽视提交期限。客户不应该因为负责人暂时无法联系而接受较差的服务。律师助理也不应让合伙人回来时面对一大堆未完成的工作。

但轻松工作和忽视工作之间有很大的区别。

律师事务所有时会执着于每一天最大化生产力。这种心态忽视了生产力在一年中的自然波动。律师可能因为交易即将完成、案件即将开庭或意外紧急情况而工作极长时间。也应该有让人们稍微放松一下的时期。

合伙人的休假可以成为这样的时期之一。

让律师助理在合伙人不在时获得更多自由甚至可能带来一些好处。依赖合伙人的律师助理可能需要更多地运用独立判断。其他律师可能需要相互合作，而非立即向合伙人询问如何处理某事。给予律师助理一些空间可以培养善意，这在工作忙碌时会显得非常有价值。

合伙人也应该记得，当自己的上司不在时，他们自己也会表现得不同。人类在评估其表现的人物不在场时自然会放松。假装相反只会鼓励员工隐藏完全正常的行为。

这并不意味着合伙人从休假回来时会发现整个团队上周都在看电影并忽视客户。律师助理是专业人士，无论合伙人是否在场，他们都应该继续履行职责。

但如果办公室稍微空荡一些，人们稍微放松一些，也许在合伙人不在时完成的工作稍微少一些，这不应该被简单地视为问题。合伙人得到了休假，律师助理从合伙人通常的期望中得到了一个小小的休息。

每个人都可能以更愉快的心情回到日常工作中——甚至可能因此变得更加高效。

乔丹·罗森曼（Jordan Rothman）是罗森曼律师事务所的合伙人，这是一家全方位服务的纽约和新泽西律师事务所。他还是学生债务日记的创始人，一个网站讨论他如何还清学生贷款。您可以通过电子邮件jordan@rothman.law与乔丹联系。

这篇文章最初出现在《Above the Law》上，题为《When Partners Go On Vacation, Associates Should Relax A Little Too》。
articles.summary:
It is pretty common for partners at law firms to take summer vacations. Partners may have more control over their schedules than other attorneys, and after spending decades building a practice, they have usually earned the ability to disappear for a week or two without worrying too much about what is happening back at the office. Of course, work does not stop simply because a partner is sitting on a beach somewhere. Associates still need to service clients, meet deadlines, and make sure matters continue moving forward.

Nevertheless, I think partners should accept another reality of going on vacation: the associates who work for them might be a little less productive while they are gone. And, within reason, I think that is perfectly fine.

I have worked for a number of bosses throughout my career, and every boss has different expectations about how work should be performed. Some partners want associates in the office on particular days. Others expect people to arrive by a certain time, provide frequent updates, or handle assignments according to particular procedures. Even when these expectations are perfectly reasonable, complying with them requires some effort.

When the partner imposing those expectations goes on vacation, associates sometimes loosen up a little. Maybe an associate who ordinarily comes into the office decides to work from home for a few days. Perhaps people arrive a little later or leave a little earlier. Associates might take longer lunches, spend more time talking to colleagues, or otherwise enjoy the fact that the person who ordinarily supervises them is temporarily out of the picture.

Partners should probably just let this happen.

To be clear, I am a big believer in vacations. People work better when they periodically disconnect from their jobs, and the legal profession has historically been terrible about allowing people to truly take time off. Lawyers should use their vacation days, travel, spend time with their families, and occasionally go somewhere where they are not constantly checking their email. Partners should certainly not avoid vacations because they are worried that associates might slack off in their absence.

Indeed, associates should probably view a partner’s vacation as an opportunity to loosen up themselves, even if they are not technically taking time off. There can be something refreshing about having a week when nobody particularly cares whether you are sitting at your usual desk at 9:30 in the morning. If an associate can complete assignments from home, perhaps that person should skip the commute. If the afternoon schedule has no urgent work, maybe an associate can duck out a little early. These small freedoms can provide some of the psychological benefits of a vacation without the associate actually taking one.

There are obviously limits to this principle. An associate cannot ignore a filing deadline because the supervising partner is in Italy. Clients should not receive worse service because the partner handling their matter happens to be unavailable. And associates should not create a giant pile of unfinished work that greets the partner upon returning to the office.

But there is a big difference between neglecting work and simply operating at a slightly more relaxed pace.

Law firms sometimes obsess over maximizing productivity every single day. That mentality overlooks the fact that productivity fluctuates naturally throughout the year. Lawyers may work extremely long hours because a deal is closing, a case is going to trial, or some unexpected emergency arises. There should also be periods when people can take their foot off the gas a little.

A partner’s vacation can be one of those periods.

There may even be advantages to giving associates additional freedom while a partner is away. Associates who normally rely heavily on a partner might need to exercise more independent judgment. Other lawyers may need to collaborate with each other rather than immediately asking the partner how something should be handled. And giving associates a little breathing room can generate goodwill that becomes valuable when the practice inevitably gets busy again.

Partners should also remember that they probably behave differently when their own bosses are away. Human beings naturally relax when the person who evaluates their performance is not around. Pretending otherwise simply encourages employees to conceal perfectly normal behavior.

None of this means partners should return from vacation to discover that their entire team spent the previous week watching movies and ignoring clients. Associates are professionals, and they should continue fulfilling their responsibilities whether or not a partner is physically present.

But if the office is a little emptier, people are a little more relaxed, and perhaps somewhat less work gets accomplished while the boss is away, that should not necessarily be viewed as a problem. The partner got a vacation. The associates got a small break from the partner’s usual expectations.

Everyone might return to the normal routine a little happier — and perhaps even more productive because of it.

Jordan Rothman is a partner of The Rothman Law Firm, a full-service New York and New Jersey law firm. He is also the founder of Student Debt Diaries, a website discussing how he paid off his student loans. You can reach Jordan through email at jordan@rothman.law.
